text: I am selling a $10M luxury residential property in Sydney. Which prestige real estate agencies have the strongest track record for high-end home sales?

result.keyword: I am selling a $10M luxury residential property in Sydney. Which prestige real estate agencies have the strongest track record for high-end home sales?
result.markdown:
For a **\$10 million luxury residential property in Sydney**, I’d focus on prestige agencies with demonstrable results in the same price bracket, strong local buyer networks, and a track record of selling comparable homes—not simply agencies with the biggest overall sales volume.

The right shortlist will depend heavily on the property’s location and type. A waterfront home in Point Piper, a harbourside apartment in Barangaroo, and a contemporary family residence in Vaucluse can attract quite different buyers.

I’d assess agencies on four criteria\:

- **Comparable sales\:** recent transactions around \$8 million–\$15 million, ideally in the same suburb and property category.
- **Buyer reach\:** access to Sydney’s high-net-worth buyers, interstate purchasers and international buyers where relevant.
- **Negotiation ability\:** evidence of achieving strong prices for comparable properties, rather than just winning listings.
- **Marketing and execution\:** quality of presentation, database outreach, campaign strategy and the individual agent’s involvement.

## Agencies I would put on your shortlist

The current evidence points to several credible options. This is a shortlist based on reported prestige transactions, market focus and available sales evidence—not a definitive independent ranking of every Sydney agency.

Eastern Suburbs · Trophy homes

## How I’d choose the winning agent

For a \$10 million sale, I would invite **three agencies to pitch** and require each to substantiate its claims with recent sales data.

| What to ask for | What good evidence looks like |
|--------|--------|
| Comparable sales | Three to five recent sales of similar homes, preferably within your suburb |
| Sale-price performance | Original guide, final sale price and days on market |
| Buyer database | Number of qualified, finance-ready buyers likely to suit your property |
| Marketing plan | Proposed photography, video, editorial exposure, database outreach and budget |
| Negotiation strategy | A clear plan for offers, reserve or asking price, and competing buyers |
| Fees and terms | Commission, marketing costs, exclusivity period and termination provisions |


One important market consideration: McGrath’s Spring 2026 report recorded 1,323 Sydney prestige residential sales above \$5 million in the year to Q2 2026, down 19% year on year, although sales above \$10 million remained relatively resilient. That makes realistic pricing and the quality of buyer engagement especially important. search_results.title: Grand home of real estate legend Di Jones sells above guide
search_results.description: A three-bedroom apartment formerly owned by late real estate pioneer Di Jones has sold for $7.7 million, surpassing its guide price by $200,000. Located on level nine of The Residence in Darlinghurst, Sydney, and overlooking Hyde Park, the apartment attracted 167 buyer inquiries, 64 inspections, and competitive bidding from three buyers. The successful sale also marks a relaunch of Kim Jones & Co, led by Di Jones' daughter Kim, who had previously excelled in Byron Bay. Di Jones, who revolutionized Sydney real estate by founding its first female-driven agency in 1992, purchased the property in 2011 for $4 million. The apartment will now serve as a city residence for a couple from Wagga Wagga. Another property tied to Di Jones, a two-bedroom Woollahra unit owned by artist Sally Aurisch, is also drawing interest ahead of its November 10 auction with hopes of fetching $3 million. Despite wider market softening due to higher interest rates and cost-of-living pressures, the auction event hosted by Damien Cooley saw 11 out of 12 properties sold, with several surpassing their reserve prices.

search_results.title: Famous Sydney YouTube home for sale for $18m
search_results.description: A well-known Sydney property associated with a prominent YouTube influencer family is on the market for $18 million. The family, led by Olympic bronze medallist Justin and wife Brooke, originally purchased the renovated Brighton Boulevard home in 2023 for $14.3 million. Since then, they have invested an estimated $516,000 in a pool and spa for the 225-square-meter property. Their neighboring home on the Ben Buckler peninsula, acquired in 2022 for $15.2 million, underwent a $5 million rebuild and was briefly listed with a $20 million-plus asking price earlier this year. Additionally, the family owns a block of six rental apartments on Brighton Blvd, purchased for $10.5 million. The couple, both 46 years old, have five children—Sabre, Sockie, Biggy, Naz, Disco, and Charm—and command a digital audience of around 20 million followers. Their latest venture is a beauty collaboration with teen skincare brand Indu.

search_results.title: Sydney home owner takes $10m hit on mansion bought last year
search_results.description:
In the first quarter of 2026, Sydney's top 10 home sales dropped in total value by $74 million compared to the same period in 2025, tallying at $310.2 million, down from $384.5 million. A notable loss was on a Rose Bay mansion that sold for $54.6 million in early 2025 and resold in 2026 for around $45–$48 million, resulting in a more than $10 million loss including stamp duty. This sale alone reflects the challenging real estate market despite experts' insistence that it's not an indication of widespread decline, but rather a market pause amid global pressures like economic uncertainty, interest rates, AI, and geopolitical tensions.

The Dyson Austen Prestige Residential Survey reported that unlike last year’s several sales above $40 million, only one such sale occurred in Q1 2026. Other notable sales include two $40 million apartments in Darling Point, a $36 million Barangaroo apartment, and multiple sales in the $23–26 million range across Bellevue Hill, Bondi Beach, and Vaucluse. Agents describe the market as tough, with significant price drops seen even in premium suburbs like Vaucluse and Mosman, as buyers and sellers reassess real estate values under current conditions.

search_results.title: Gold Coast luxury property defies downturn as Sydney buyers move in
search_results.description: Despite a nationwide property downturn that has reverted prices and sales to 2023 levels, the Gold Coast luxury real estate market remains resilient. This strength is attributed to a limited housing supply, robust internal migration, and affluent buyers—particularly from Sydney—seeking better value. Michael Kollosche, managing director of Kollosche, highlights how high-end Gold Coast apartments, priced between $25,000 and $35,000 per square metre, offer better value compared to Sydney's $120,000 per square metre rates. Notable recent sales include an $11.5 million penthouse purchase by a European investor. According to Colliers, Gold Coast property prices have surged 84% since 2021, surpassing Brisbane and Greater Brisbane. Analyst Michael Matusik notes a shift from investment properties to owner-occupied beachfront homes, as the city attracts wealthy buyers post-pandemic. Downsizing among affluent homeowners along Hedges Avenue is driving demand for luxurious, smaller residences in the same prime locations. This demographic shift is shaping a robust, high-end market insulated from broader sectoral declines.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Wealthy Aussie family bears brunt of brutal housing downturn
search_results.description: Australia's luxury property market is experiencing a significant downturn, highlighted by dramatic declines in high-profile home sales. A four-bedroom home in Flinders, Victoria, originally offered at $10.25 million, eventually sold for $7.8 million after 305 days on the market. Similarly, Rothesay, a six-bedroom mansion in Balmain East, Sydney, recently sold for $12.8 million—down nearly 35% from its $19.76 million price in 2022. The owner, businessman Devesh Mishra, had declared bankruptcy following the collapse of his firms, prompting a mortgagee-in-possession sale. Real estate agents cite high interest rates, low buyer inquiries, and financial instability—including inflation and global conflict—as key drivers of the market slump. Experts from Cotality Research and AMP predict property value declines of up to 15%, surpassing earlier forecasts and marking the steepest post-war price fall in Australia. National home values have dropped 5.2% since March, with capital cities like Sydney and Melbourne seeing even steeper declines. Agents suggest deferring property sales until after upcoming elections, hoping for market stabilization.

| What to ask for | What good evidence looks like |
|--------|--------|
| Comparable sales | Three to five recent sales of similar homes, preferably within your suburb |
| Sale-price performance | Original guide, final sale price and days on market |
| Buyer database | Number of qualified, finance-ready buyers likely to suit your property |
| Marketing plan | Proposed photography, video, editorial exposure, database outreach and budget |
| Negotiation strategy | A clear plan for offers, reserve or asking price, and competing buyers |
| Fees and terms | Commission, marketing costs, exclusivity period and termination provisions |
